parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented targeting, and no universal-exposure measure (no facility ban, no marker rule, no custody practice) appear — the resident-facing gaps (no LGR, no enumerated anti-discrimination ground, no domestic marriage route) are not visitor exposures. Documented positives: a functioning appellate court invoking equality, immigration recognition of an overseas marriage, and broad official participation (premier, governor, ministers) in a 600-person Pride — real evidence of institutional tolerance in a small territory where a single incident would carry weight, yet none is recorded. Offset downward: public expression is 'arranged rather than free-standing' (organisers capped displays of affection), a 2009 constitutional carve-out, and the marriage ban restored on appeal — mild social-friction/hostility signals. No service-protection enforcement for trans visitors is documented, so it sits a step below the acceptance-with-working-remedies tier. Thin data, extrapolated from the functioning-court and official-visibility record, not to the midpoint.
